text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a 3px focus ring to every interactive element that gets keyboard focus. This makes the target visible for keyboard users without cluttering the UI for mouse users. The trade-off is a tiny bit of extra visual noise, but it’s worth it for the 10% of users who rely on keyboards.

name: Reader
text: Risk: A 3px ring with 4px offset still risks vanishing on dark or patterned backdrops, breaking WCAG 2.2 AA. Better: Use a 4px ring with 2px offset—it survives dark themes and meets 4.5:1 contrast. Settle it: Test the ring on a dark background and a busy pattern; if it fails, switch to a 4px ring with 2px offset.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a 4px focus ring with a 2px offset to every interactive element that gets keyboard focus. This ring will survive dark backgrounds and busy patterns while meeting WCAG 2.2 AA contrast requirements. The trade-off is slightly more visual noise for mouse users, but it ensures keyboard navigators can always see where they are without fail.

name: Reader
text: Risk: A 4px ring with 2px offset still risks failing 4.5:1 contrast on dark backdrops if the ring color isn’t carefully chosen. Better: Use a semi-transparent ring (e.g., 30% opacity) that adapts to background contrast—test it on dark, light, and patterned surfaces. Settle it: Measure contrast ratios in a tool like WebAIM’s Contrast Checker; if any fail, switch to a solid ring with a darker/lighter fallback color.
